messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail spike detected on continuous-batching streaming path in prod-usw2 — p99 jumped from 220ms -> 2.3s over last 10m. Auto-mitigation triggered: preemptive-shed=off, fallback routing=disabled. Paging oncall.
sasha: oncall here. seeing p95 ~ 480ms, p99 ~ 2.3s. topology: mixed-tenant traffic, a few tenants with long seqs (~>3k tokens) causing packing to pad. streaming stalls + occasional 502 from grpc-forwarder. paging now.
devon: looking at console -> per-route breakdown: /v1/stream-gen has 65% of p99 traffic, batch size distribution skewed: many batches with 1 long seq + small seqs -> GPU kernel path falling back to slower attention on long sequences. KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% for those tenants.
kevin: also seeing scheduler fairness skew. Long-seq requests are holding slots and preventing packer from combining many small short requests. suspected cause: preemptive preemption not firing because seq-length metadata missing on some headers.
maria: customer impact? any external alerts yet?
lee: Pager shows 3 customers with increased error rates (timeouts) — affected endpoints: streaming & streaming-chunked. Errors mostly timeouts for >10s then grpc reset. No broad loss of traffic, but spikes correspond to tails.
pagerduty-bot: INC-9876 opened and assigned to eng-oncall. Severity: Sev2. Notifying customer-facing.
sasha: quick mitigation ideas: 1) enable model-variant fallback to lower-memory quantized variant for long sequences; 2) reduce max_batch_size from 32 -> 12 for streaming worker pool; 3) enable seqlen-based preemptive-shed (shed >2k tokens) temporarily; 4) route flagged tenants to dedicated pool if we have capacity.
devon: agree. I can push a runtime flag to reduce max_batch_size on the streaming replicas. that's low-risk and reversible. prepping patch: git sha abc1234 -> config: stream.max_batch_size=12. will roll to us-west-2 edge.
kevin: I can flip seqlen-based preemptive-shed experiment flag in feature gates: runtime.feature.seqlen_shed=true; threshold=2048. Note: this requires seqlen header which some older clients don't send — we can estimate by tokenization heuristic in the packer as fallback.
maria: coordinate customer comms: if we route a customer to dedicated capacity temporarily, they'll see improved latency but might be billed differently. cc @support.
lee: operational checklist: - apply max_batch_size change (devon) - enable seqlen_shed (kevin) - enable fallback routing to quantized model (sasha) - monitor p95/p99 and error-rate for next 30m - if not improved, consider KV-cache eviction + restart of a few streaming workers.
sasha: devon, please run the batch-size change now and roll canary to 10% of streaming workers.
devon: rolling canary now -> command: kubectl set env deploy/stream-worker STREAM_MAX_BATCH=12 --record; rolling 10% canary: rollout canary label=contbatch-mitig-canary=1/10
kevin: enabling seqlen_shed flag now. command: curl -XPOST https://ops-api/internal/feature-gates -d '{"key":"seqlen_shed","on":true,"threshold":2048}'
kevin: note: will also enable estimate_seqlen=true to cover missing headers.
sasha: enabling model fallback: route policy update -> policy engine: add fallback_rule for long-seq tenants -> model_variant: redwood-lite-4qint8. this reduces perf but reduces OOM/kernel fallback.
lee: metrics update: after canary applied (2m) p95 dropped to 300ms, p99 down to 620ms on canary hosts. Small improvement, good sign.
maria: customer impact update: notified affected customers that we're investigating with mitigation steps. will prepare a short status message if p99 doesn't recover to <500ms in 15m.
devon: expanding canary to 40% now. rolling.
kevin: after enabling seqlen_shed + estimate_seqlen, background: packer now preempts long seqs into separate batches instead of waiting. p99 globally dropped to ~480ms after 6m.
sasha: good. keep watch for any regressions — packing changes can increase cost due to more small batches.
lee: alerting: new spikes seen at 16:38 UTC on region prod-eu due to different tenant mix. seems similar pattern; will apply same config there.
pagerduty-bot: Update: INC-9876 state changed -> mitigated_by_eng. Followup: post-incident report required.
maria: Action items for postmortem: - root cause: mixing long-seq tenants + missing seqlen headers + scheduler fairness bug. - mitigation: enforce seqlen header, enable server-side seq estimation, tune default max_batch_size per workload, add tenant-level routing for heavy long-seq usage, implement admission control to avoid single long seq blocking many short requests. - customer follow-up owners assigned: maria -> draft message; support -> reach out to 3 customers.
kevin: long-term: we should implement token-aware fair scheduler that accounts for seqlen in slot allocation, plus a knob for max-packing-wait-time. add to runtime roadmap.
devon: rolling back temporary flags once stable. will revert canary labels and keep seqlen_shed in experiment mode until next patch.
sasha: closing notes: system stabilized for now, p99 back to ~420-500ms, errors dropped to baseline. keep 1hr watch and then hand off to infra oncall for followup.
lee: handoff: paging oncall-infra for 1hr monitoring -> @infra-oncall
sasha: thanks team. I'll file the incident doc and assign postmortem owners.
summary: Continuous-batching streaming path p99 spike due to mixed sequence lengths and missing seqlen headers; live mitigations: reduce max_batch_size, enable seqlen-based preemptive shedding (with estimation), enable model fallback for long sequences, canary rollouts; customer notifications and postmortem actions assigned.
